detailedSectionAnalyses.title: Training methodology
detailedSectionAnalyses.intro: Eight pages sit in this grouping on All other content. They largely share a single Nose to Nose teaching philosophy, but differ in language, completeness, and how much they repeat one another.

mainPoints.heading: Philosophy of facilitation
bullets: Facilitators stay true to clowning by following each person’s creative process, not imposing a fixed technique.
The work nurtures emotional expression and imagination, and helps each participant find their own clown — unique to them and rooted in their relationship with the audience.
Focusing on the individual is presented as the heart of clowning: a search for authenticity in both personal and social life.

mainPoints.heading: Who it’s for and why people return
bullets: The approach is framed as relevant to personal growth (“Clown Within”) and social mediation (Court Jester Group).
Workshops welcome people of all ages and backgrounds, with or without theatre experience.
Many participants return because the freedom and playfulness of the work becomes essential to them.

mainPoints.heading: What happens in a workshop
bullets: Groups are capped at 12 participants.
Sessions use warm-up games, vocal and physical exercises, then stage improvisations (solo or with others).
After each improvisation, the group discusses what worked — to draw out the positive, distinctive qualities of each person’s clown.
This happens within clear rules intended to create a safe, respectful, protective environment.

mainPoints.heading: The “inner clown”
bullets: The red nose is described as “the smallest mask in the world” and “the mask that unmasks.”
Clown work rediscovers openness, spontaneity, and play.
Imagination is encouraged while staying grounded; the inner clown emerges through improvisation and welcoming whatever arises.

mainPoints.heading: Eight committed teaching principles
mainPoints.note: On principles pages and in full on the German page.
bullets: Small groups — max 12, so everyone gets solo/pair time, individual coaching, and no competition for space.
Person-centred approach — authenticity and inner experience matter more than acquiring external skills.
Structured, level-appropriate teaching — groups formed by experience; curriculum introduced clearly; team meets regularly to refine methods.
Committed guidance and support — facilitators accompany participants gently through difficulty and foster collaborative enquiry.
Positive regard — feedback highlights what is working; a supportive environment is seen as essential to clowning courage.
Learners as their own teachers — reflection after exercises, games, and improvisations is treated as the most important part of learning.
Collaborative research — many courses use two facilitators to bring diversity and continuity.
Personal and social voice — clowns are not silent mimes; the work uses language, full emotional range, body, and voice, with a safety rule: never hurt yourself or others, and don’t break anything.

mainPoints.heading: Italian page only: progression through levels 1–3
bullets: Level 1 — grounds clowning in authenticity, presence, playfulness, and trust; helps overcome fears that block being in the moment.
Level 2 — focuses on structure and relationships: awareness of partners, images, stories, characters, and audience; more rigorous improvisation.
Level 3 — examines strategies used to avoid mistakes; uses repetition and theatrical technique; moves toward performance.

duplication.heading: Near-verbatim duplicates (English)
bullets: approach = uk/our-approach-2 = nax/approach-na — three copies of the same “Our approach” text (philosophy, workshop format, Clown Within).
principles = uk/our-principles — two copies of the same eight principles and their expanded explanations.

duplication.heading: Cross-language versions of the same material
bullets: de/herangehensweise is essentially the German translation of both the approach page and the principles page combined — including workshop format, inner clown, and all eight principles with full explanations.
pl/approach is a short Polish summary: principle headings plus the core philosophy paragraphs, without the detailed expansions.
it/metodo largely repeats the approach/workshop/inner-clown content in Italian, but is the only page in this group that also includes level 1–3 progression detail.

duplication.heading: Conceptual overlap between page types
bullets: The opening philosophy in the “approach” pages repeats ideas that reappear inside the “person-centred approach” principle.
“What happens in a workshop” and “small groups (max 12)” appear in both approach pages and the principles section — stated twice on de/herangehensweise because it merges both sources.
Links on UK/international pages point to separate progression/course pages that cover material partially duplicated on it/metodo.

detailedSectionAnalyses.conclusion: This grouping is really two core English documents (Approach + Principles), replicated across UK, international, and North America legacy sites, then translated or abbreviated for Germany, Italy, and Poland. Consolidating to one canonical approach page and one principles page per language would remove most redundancy; the Italian level descriptions are the main unique addition not found elsewhere in this group.

detailedSectionAnalyses.title: Training programme
detailedSectionAnalyses.intro: Eleven pages sit in this grouping. They describe course formats, the two-year training outline, and level-by-level progression — often repeating the same level descriptions across international, UK, and German sites.

mainPoints.heading: Two-year programme
bullets: Nose to Nose offers a coherent two-year programme from basics through performance and Social Clowning.
Participants can choose their own pace but two years is recommended for integration.
Basic training: Clown 1 (one week or 3 weekends), Clown 2, Clown 3, five Performance weekends, and Social Clowning (one week).

mainPoints.heading: Course formats
bullets: Introductory days (1–2 days) — light introduction to presence and the unexpected.
Special theme weekends (2–3 days) — cross-disciplinary research with conflict, biography, ecology, meditation, storytelling, therapy, etc.
Ongoing weekends (4–6 per year) — same group, building depth month by month.
Intensive residential weeks (~7 hours/day) — full immersion at levels 1–3.
Workshops also run outside the UK (Germany, France, Italy, Switzerland, US); groups capped at 12 unless stated otherwise.

mainPoints.heading: Level 1 — Courage to Be
bullets: Grounds clowning in presence and authenticity; nurtures each person’s unique clown through listening and receptivity.
Connects to playful spirit; develops trust in self and life.
Inward process focused on overcoming fears that block being in the “Here and Now.”

mainPoints.heading: Level 2 — Embracing the Unexpected
bullets: Shifts focus to structure and relationship — partner, audience, images, stories, characters.
Teaching changes to deepen improvisation and performance technique; new structures bring greater rigour.

mainPoints.heading: Level 3 — The Wisdom of Imperfection
bullets: Examines strategies for avoiding mistakes; greater theatrical and improvisational technique.
Improvs repeated in less comfortable areas; moves toward performance.

mainPoints.heading: Towards Performance
bullets: Practice improvising before a real audience; includes public performances.
Group revisits improvs with insights from each performance.
Introduces key principles of Social Clowning.

mainPoints.heading: Social Clowning
bullets: Draws on Court Jester and Fool traditions.
Aims to renew creative processes and bring playful irreverence to relationships and institutions.
Practices mirroring social/symbolic references, reclaiming paradox, parodying power, celebrating the heart.
Clown holds a mirror to life, puts the human heart at the centre, and speaks truths others cannot.

mainPoints.heading: Historical / regional-only content
bullets: nax/two-year-clown-training — 2013–15 North America launch with pricing and application details (partially broken markup).
uk/uk-clown-facilitator-training and uk/facilitators-in-training-2012-14 — records of a past facilitator training cohort, not part of the public progression path.

duplication.heading: Near-verbatim duplicates
bullets: progression = uk/the-nose-to-nose-progression — identical level 1 through Social Clowning descriptions.
de/kursstufen = de/archives/175 — same German level content on two URLs.

duplication.heading: Split across pages (international English)
bullets: two-year-training-programme holds the programme intro and outline; progression holds level detail; courseguideline holds format types — three pages that together form one training guide.
Level descriptions also appear inside it/metodo (Training methodology group) for levels 1–3 only.

duplication.heading: Cross-language versions
bullets: de/kursstufen translates the progression levels for Germany.
it/formazione and itx/formazione are Italian programme overviews on current and legacy sites.

detailedSectionAnalyses.conclusion: The international English training story is really three complementary pages (programme outline, course formats, level progression) plus near-identical UK copies. Consolidating to one training programme page per language would cover the full path from introductory day to Social Clowning; facilitator-training and regional launch announcements are historical records rather than core programme content.

detailedSectionAnalyses.title: Applied clowning
detailedSectionAnalyses.intro: Six pages describe bringing clowning beyond the training room — into organisations, wellbeing, and social settings. English sources are short; German pages carry the most detailed corporate and burnout-prevention offerings.

pages.role: Core essay — play, communication, areas of work

mainPoints.heading: Philosophy of applied clowning
bullets: “Play is wiser than words” — through play we learn about the world, others, self, and communication.
Nose to Nose has worked with teachers, social workers, doctors, nurses, and therapists over many years.

mainPoints.heading: Areas of work
bullets: Social Clowning — events, conferences, meetings (see dedicated offering below).
Teacher training.
Conflict and communication.
Personal development.
Special needs (mentioned on Italian stub only in this group).

mainPoints.heading: Social Clowning for organisations
bullets: Facilitators attend as “normal” guests, observe, then offer 5–10 minute skits summarising key ideas — like Court Jesters.
Up to four “reviews” per day event.
Brings cheekiness and gentle chaos to break institutional conventions; gets people talking and reframes issues creatively.
Example: 2010 Nowhere Academy Creative Dialogue in London (video on original page).

mainPoints.heading: Custom in-house workshops
bullets: Workshops designed for specific organisations and groups on request.

de/interne-workshops lists past clients: Waldorf teacher training (Stuttgart), Goetheanum student conferences, team building (Potsdam), English/German teacher weeks, circus pedagogy (Berlin), refugee circus training, anthroposophical conferences, and more.
Recurring themes: intuitive intelligence, courage to be oneself, clown and conflict/communication/trauma.

mainPoints.heading: Burnout prevention (German page)
bullets: Addresses work pressure, double burdens, routine, miscommunication, and lack of recognition.
Uses clowning to discover resources, strengthen perception, and meet professional challenges with lightness and humour.
Target groups: doctors, teachers, managers, parents, therapists, social workers, and others under high stress.
Workshop format repeats standard Nose to Nose approach (max 12, warm-ups, improvs, discussion, inner clown).

mainPoints.heading: Integration with heart (German page)
bullets: For companies employing refugees; aims to build empathy and appreciation across language and culture barriers.
Uses theatre clowning and improvisation so employees find a shared heartfelt language.
Contact: berlin@nosetonose.de

duplication.heading: Overlap with other groups
bullets: Social Clowning level content in Training programme repeats themes from social-clowning and links from uk/applied-clowning.
Burnout prevention page reuses workshop-format and “inner clown” paragraphs from Approach/Principles (in German).
de/interne-workshops mixes bilingual intro with a long list of one-off past engagements rather than a single service description.

duplication.heading: Language split
bullets: Only uk/applied-clowning and social-clowning are substantive English pages; burnout and integration exist only in German.
it/altre-esperienze is essentially empty — a single line pointing to special needs work.

detailedSectionAnalyses.conclusion: Applied clowning content is fragmented: a short UK essay plus a full Social Clowning service page in English, with richer corporate and wellbeing detail on German pages. A consolidated applied clowning page can unite the English sources and translate the unique German offerings; the interne-workshops catalogue is reference material rather than core narrative.

detailedSectionAnalyses.title: Booking
detailedSectionAnalyses.intro: Two pages relate to booking. Only one carries practical instructions; the other is a post-registration thank-you page.

pages.role: Full booking, payment, and cancellation instructions

mainPoints.heading: How to book
bullets: Use the “Click here to enquire…” link on each course page; submit the form with your details.
Nose to Nose confirms availability and explains deposit payment.
Deposits by cheque, bank transfer, or online; booking confirmed only after deposit received.
Check total cost including accommodation and meals — booking usually covers tuition only.

mainPoints.heading: Confirmation and waiting list
bullets: A place is confirmed ONLY when Nose to Nose confirms; no deposit taken if the course is full.
Full courses → waiting list with priority when a place opens; team will try to offer the next available course.

mainPoints.heading: Practical expectations
bullets: Early booking appreciated because of venue commitments.
Groups limited to 12; places allocated in order received.
Budget separately for board and accommodation.

mainPoints.heading: Payment terms and cancellation
bullets: Cancel up to 60 days before → deposit refunded minus £20 cancellation fee.
No refunds after 60 days unless a replacement takes the place.
If Nose to Nose cancels → full refund with 14 days’ notice; travel insurance advised for long-distance travellers.

mainPoints.heading: Thank-you page (de/hurra)
bullets: Shown after successful registration on the German site — no additional booking information.

duplication.heading: Scattered booking notes
bullets: Course date pages and regional event listings repeat fragments of waiting-list and early-booking advice.
de/hurra duplicates the confirmation message implied on booking — no conflicting content.

detailedSectionAnalyses.conclusion: Booking is effectively a single international instructions page. Regional course-date pages could link to one canonical booking page; de/hurra remains a post-checkout confirmation, not part of the reader-facing guide.

mainPoints.heading: Usage and access
bullets: Articles provided for reading; readers must respect copyright and quote sources.
Some recent articles/interviews require joining the mailing list (updates twice yearly, no list sharing, easy unsubscribe).
Several older pieces available on request as PDF by email.

mainPoints.heading: Themes across the catalogue
bullets: Clowning in healthcare and GP practice (David Wheeler, David McGavin interviews and articles).
Teaching and language education (Catherine Bryden, Peter Lutzker, Robert McNeer, German teacher articles).
Psychotherapy and personal development (Rob Leiper, Bertil Sylvander, Jean-Bernard Bonange).
Organisational and systemic work (Sharon Usher on clowning and constellations).
Philosophy and archetype (Deon van Zyl on the fool; Chris Seeley PhD).
Special needs (Laura Geilen).
Research and theses (Vivian Gladwell M.A. thesis on clowning for language teachers).

mainPoints.heading: Hosted vs external articles
bullets: Many full texts are scraped to content/articles/ (bertilarticle, catherinebryden, seeley, etc.).
Others link externally (BMJ Careers, GP Online, blog posts, Clean Language site, Sheridan Hill website).
“Articles coming up” entries point to placeholder sorry page.

mainPoints.heading: Italian and German unique content
bullets: Italian site hosts full translations of key articles not always linked from English indexes.
de/artikel is press coverage; de/clowning-fur-lehrer and de/was/burnout-prevention are standalone articles miscategorised under Articles or Applied clowning.
pl/articles-3 is a short Polish landing page rather than a full catalogue.

duplication.heading: Near-verbatim duplicates (English)
bullets: articles = uk/articles = na/articles — same chronological catalogue with the same entries and descriptions.
International legacy articles.htm matches the WordPress articles pages.

duplication.heading: Cross-listing
bullets: Several articles also appear as individual scraped article pages under content/articles/.
de/was/burnout-prevention is a full article but categorised under Articles; topic overlaps Applied clowning.
David Wheeler appears in multiple entries across years (2001, 2004, 2008, 2014).

detailedSectionAnalyses.conclusion: The English articles story is one index page replicated three times, linking to a mix of on-site articles and external publications. A consolidated articles page should preserve the copyright note, chronological catalogue, and links to hosted content; Italian and German articles remain language-specific extensions rather than duplicates of the English list.
